title: Why Emily from "Corpse Bride" is one of my favorite film characters of all time.

commenti.body:
(Part 2)

As Barkins witnesses this, he accepts defeat and mocks Emily for never finding her love and being dead as he toasts with the poison that was meant for Victor. Barkins, as a result, dies from the poison and is dragged to the underworld, where he will most likely be punished the horrible things that he did.

Now that she is freed from the trauma of the person who has caused her death and has learned to let go of Victor by allowing him to be with the person he loves, she has now found fulfillment and becomes into a bunch of butterflies flying into the moonlight, symbolizing her ascending to her happy place, liberated from her pain and the need to find someone to keep her happy.

Paradoxically, Emily finds happiness by giving away her happiness. By letting the person she loves be happy, that is enough to make her happy herself. And I feel that also, in a way, part of the reason this makes her feel better is because somebody else has found what she couldn't find and that she has permitted for other people to have found that for themselves. It's a rather sad but also very sweet conclusion for Emily. She does not become the bride but the bridesmaid like Barkins said but her heart hasn't stopped beating nor does it need to be broken. Her only stopped beating when she held that heart for someone who didn't need her heart and she gave it back to herself by coming to this fact.

I find her story very inspiring because I understand very much how hard it is to let go of someone who means a lot to you but doesn't return those feelings back to you. It is not easy to accept and you try so hard for things to come to an agreement where we can be together. But the more you try and try to pressure and hold on to that heart, the more it sinks and drowns and that love grows weaker and weaker until it becomes empty. The guilt comes and you are now with someone who just isn't happy. And neither are you happy. The heart stops beating for them and for you. So the best is to just... let go.

If you give your heart to someone who won't protect it for you, you're never getting it back. That is what happened when she offered herself to Barkins and it is what happened when she tried to marry Victor when he had somebody else.

So what happens if your happiness prevents someone else's happiness? Well, you just find your own on your own. It may take time to get used to but eventually, there will come a time where we can be happy with that choice and by letting them live their life.

Also, this may be a bit of a stretch but I think there's some interest symbolism with the maggot living inside Emily and the ending. At first, the maggot keeps living inside her and being annoying but later on in the movie, it decides to stop living inside her and later becomes into a bunch of butterflies which are now freed from being a living corpse with Beatles heart.
